value_source: ABS, Creating a child mobility indicator using the Life Course Dataset
variable_description: The address a person lived at, held as a key rather than as text. In plida_core_loc and the per-source address tables one row is one episode: the person was at this address from START_DATE to END_DATE, and the MB, SA1, SA2 and SA4 columns beside it are that address geocoded. The ar_addr table is the other side of the join, holding one row per address with its use and its dwelling structure, so the identifier is what turns a location episode into a described dwelling. Because the key is the address and not the person, everyone living there carries the same value, and SOURCE_FLAG records which agency's records the episode was drawn from.
description_source: ABS, Creating a child mobility indicator using the Life Course Dataset
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for an address, not for a person, a household or a dwelling, so a shared value shows co-residence rather than a relationship. An administrative address is only as current as the person's last dealing with the agency, so an episode can outlast a move. ABS found that 4.3% to 11.2% of children with an address history between 2006 and 2021 were missing an ARID, and the version of Core Locations used for the child mobility indicator imputes those gaps. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions, so a shared value is strong evidence of a shared address rather than proof of one.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL names the field Address Register ID. ABS documents the Core Locations module as holding a secure hashed ARID standing for each address in the ABS Address Register, and describes the address history structure (ARID with start and end dates of residence) that the registry's own table layout shows: SPINE_ID, ARID, START_DATE, END_DATE and the ASGS codings, with ar_addr holding address use and dwelling structure against the same key.
evidence_quote: a secure hashed Address Register Identifier (ARID) that represents each address in the ABS Address Register
supersedes_rationale: The domain was marked guessed with the generic sentence 'The domain is open, so no finite value list applies.' ABS publishes what the identifier is and how it is de-identified, which makes the domain sourced and lets the entry say what the column is for.
